objective.value: Engineer an Escherichia coli strain capable of growing on CO2 and formic acid (FA) alone to a higher cell density than previously reported engineered strains (prior reported final OD600 up to ~1), as a potential platform strain for bio-based production of chemicals solely from CO2 and FA.
objective.notes: Objective stated in abstract and introduction of the current article.

value: H1 (authors' hypothesis): the inability of strain FC1 to grow solely on CO2 and FA might be due to insufficient gluconeogenesis, simultaneous expression of the purT and ftl genes, and inefficient NADPH supply.
H2 (authors' hypothesis): excessive plasmid gene expression might negatively affect cell growth during limited nutrient supply in a medium containing CO2 and FA alone.

H3 (authors' hypothesis): cell filamentation of FC8 might be due to energy deficiency when growing on CO2 and FA alone; reducing cultivation temperature might improve energy efficiency by increasing cytochrome bo (Cyo) and decreasing cytochrome bd-I (Cyd) ubiquinol oxidase expression.
hypothesis.notes: These are author-stated hypotheses (author_interpretation), phrased with 'might'; they are not validated mechanisms. H3 was later supported by biomass-yield and mRNA measurements, but causal validation of the full mechanism (e.g., direct ATP measurement) is not reported.

value: FC1 failed to grow on CO2 and FA alone (Fig. 1b)

After IPTG/aeration optimization, FC5 grew to OD600 0.533 in 200 h from initial OD600 0.07 (reported as 0.87-fold higher than 0.285)

FC8 (low-copy plasmid) grew to OD600 0.607 in 200 h from initial OD600 0.06 (0.14-fold higher than FC5); FC7 reached OD600 0.452; CO2/FA assimilation fluxes and FA consumption of FC8 exceeded those of FC5
FC8 from initial OD600 0.35 grew to OD600 1.24 (0.343 g DCW/L) in 100 h; cells were filamented, proposed as one reason growth stopped

At 32 °C, FC8 grew from OD600 0.31 to 2.48 (0.687 g DCW/L) in 244 h, consuming 0.41 g FA (8.2 g/L FA equivalent); cyoAB mRNA increased and cydAB mRNA decreased as intended vs 37 °C; biomass yields on FA were 0.0552 ± 0.0009 (32 °C) vs 0.0365 ± 0.0026 (37 °C) g DCW/g FA; filamentation suppressed

From low initial OD600 0.018, FC8 grew to OD600 3.59 (0.994 g DCW/L) in 791.5 h, consuming 0.94 g FA (18.8 g/L equivalent), 7.64 doublings; specific growth rate declined from 0.0105 to 0.0028 /h and doubling time rose from 65.9 to 250.6 h

Bioreactor fed-batch from initial OD600 ~1: maximum OD600 7.38 (2.044 g DCW/L) in 450 h consuming 18.2 g FA (36.4 g/L equivalent); three independent reproductions reached OD600 7.88 (412 h), 8.01 (412 h) and 11.1 (577 h); summarized as OD600 7-11

Authors' stated limitation: low specific growth rate still needs improvement; suggested future directions (adaptive laboratory evolution, further metabolic engineering, bioreactor optimization) are proposals, not performed experiments
outcomes.notes: Outcomes are direct observations bound to their experiment instances. The authors' mechanistic interpretation (energy efficiency via Cyo/Cyd) is an author_interpretation supported by mRNA and yield data; direct ATP measurements are not reported.

ddr_annotations.decision_type_rationale: Construction of base strain DH5α_GTPS (gcvR, pflB, serA deletions; gcvT native promoter replaced with trc) is described as a pre-existing strain (Supplementary Note 3; consistent with prior work ref. 9). It fails the current-study gate and is recorded as background, not as a current-study engineering decision.
ddr_annotations.design_action: Prior construction of DH5α_GTPS (ΔgcvR ΔpflB ΔserA, PgcvT::trc)
ddr_annotations.design_action_rationale: Described only as the pre-existing recipient strain for FC1; construction details are in unavailable Supplementary Note 3.
ddr_annotations.evidence_grading_rationale: Background strain; no current-study decision to grade.
ddr_annotations.reason_nature_rationale: No rationale for the base-strain design is reported in the available text of this paper.

ddr_annotations.decision_type_rationale: Q1: active introduction of a synthetic CO2/FA assimilation pathway (reconstructed THF cycle, reverse glycine cleavage, CbFdh). Q2: performed by current authors (FC1 construction). Q3: an explicit design choice of pathway and host.
ddr_annotations.design_action: Construct strain FC1 by introducing a reconstructed THF cycle, reverse glycine cleavage reaction and Candida boidinii Fdh into E. coli DH5α_GTPS
ddr_annotations.design_action_rationale: Stated goal: engineer E. coli to grow on CO2 and FA alone; FA can be converted to reducing power by Fdh and is assimilated more efficiently than CO2 by microorganisms.
ddr_annotations.trigger_observation: Previously reported engineered E. coli strains grew on CO2 and FA only to low final OD600 (up to ~1); a strain growing to higher cell density on CO2 and FA alone was needed (Introduction, citing refs 9-11).
ddr_annotations.evidence_grading_rationale: evidence_basis_type=literature_precedent + author_assertion: pathway choice rests on cited prior studies (refs 4, 5, 9) and authors' reasoning about FA/Fdh advantages, not on new measurements made before the decision.
ddr_annotations.reason_nature_rationale: The pathway design explicitly builds on the authors' and others' prior one-carbon assimilation work cited in the Introduction.

ddr_annotations.decision_type_rationale: Q1: ppsA overexpression (promoter change) and ppsR deletion are deliberate genome edits. Q2: performed in this study (Methods). Q3: chosen to address a hypothesized limitation of FC1.
ddr_annotations.design_action: Overexpress ppsA and delete the ppsR repressor in FC1 to produce FC2
ddr_annotations.design_action_rationale: Authors hypothesized that insufficient gluconeogenesis might be one reason FC1 could not grow on CO2 and FA alone.
ddr_annotations.trigger_observation: FC1 failed to grow on CO2 and FA alone (Fig. 1b), followed by the stated hypothesis of insufficient gluconeogenesis.
ddr_annotations.evidence_grading_rationale: evidence_basis_type=author_assertion (hypothesis): the gluconeogenesis limitation was hypothesized ('might be'), not measured, before the edit; 13C isotope comparisons of FC1 vs FC2 were performed afterwards.
ddr_annotations.reason_nature_rationale: A mechanistic hypothesis (insufficient gluconeogenesis via ppsA/ppsR) was stated before the engineering action; it remains hypothesis-level reasoning, not a validated mechanism.

ddr_annotations.decision_type_rationale: Q1: targeted deletion of purT. Q2: performed in this study (Methods; host named 'AKO strain', see conflicts). Q3: chosen to address hypothesized simultaneous purT/ftl expression issue.
ddr_annotations.design_action: Delete purT in FC2 to produce FC3
ddr_annotations.design_action_rationale: Authors hypothesized that simultaneous expression of the purT and ftl genes might contribute to FC1's inability to grow on CO2 and FA.
ddr_annotations.trigger_observation: FC1 growth failure plus the stated purT/ftl co-expression hypothesis (logically prior to the deletion).
ddr_annotations.reason_nature_rationale: Mechanistic hypothesis stated before the action; not independently validated as the cause.

ddr_annotations.decision_type_rationale: Q1: introduction of plasmid p100FA2 expressing A. thaliana fdh_mut. Q2: constructed in this study. Q3: chosen to address hypothesized NADPH supply limitation.
ddr_annotations.design_action: Harbour p100FA2 in FC3 (yielding FC5) to additionally express Arabidopsis thaliana fdh_mut for NADPH generation from FA
ddr_annotations.design_action_rationale: Authors hypothesized inefficient NADPH supply as a third reason for FC1's growth failure.
ddr_annotations.trigger_observation: FC1 growth failure plus the stated NADPH-supply hypothesis (prior to constructing FC5).
ddr_annotations.evidence_grading_rationale: evidence_basis_type=author_assertion (hypothesis-level); NADPH supply was not directly measured before the decision.
ddr_annotations.reason_nature_rationale: Mechanistic hypothesis (cofactor/reducing-power balance) stated before the action.

ddr_annotations.decision_type_rationale: Q1: deliberate adjustment of IPTG inducer concentration and aeration. Q2: performed in this study (Extended Data Fig. 5). Q3: a process-optimization design choice selected from tested conditions.
ddr_annotations.design_action: Optimize IPTG concentration (tested 1, 0.1, 0.05 mM) and aeration condition (three flask formats) for FC5 cultivation
ddr_annotations.design_action_rationale: Goal: enable cells to grow to a higher density after FC5 first grew on CO2+FA.
ddr_annotations.trigger_observation: FC5 grew on CO2 and FA alone but only to OD600 0.285 in 150 h, motivating optimization to reach higher density.
ddr_annotations.evidence_grading_rationale: evidence_basis_type=screening_result / experimental_measurement: conditions were compared experimentally (Extended Data Fig. 5a-c); however, the final selected IPTG concentration is not stated in the available text (Supplementary Note 6 missing).
ddr_annotations.reason_nature_rationale: The optimized condition was derived from experimental comparison of inducer concentrations and aeration levels.
alternatives_considered: IPTG 1 mM, 0.1 mM, 0.05 mM and high/medium/low aeration were compared; the selected values are not identifiable from the available text

ddr_annotations.decision_type_rationale: Q1: plasmid copy-number reduction via reconstructed medium-/low-copy plasmids. Q2: performed in this study (p184FA, p518FA construction; FC7/FC8). Q3: explicit design choice to fine-tune plasmid gene expression.
ddr_annotations.design_action: Fine-tune plasmid gene expression by moving the C1 pathway operon from the high-copy plasmid in FC5 to medium-copy (FC7) and low-copy (FC8) plasmids
ddr_annotations.design_action_rationale: Authors reasoned that excessive gene expression might negatively affect cell growth during limited nutrient supply in CO2/FA-only medium.
ddr_annotations.trigger_observation: FC5 grew only to OD600 0.533 even after IPTG/aeration optimization, together with the prior hypothesis that excessive plasmid gene expression burdens growth under nutrient limitation.
ddr_annotations.evidence_grading_rationale: evidence_basis_type=author_assertion (hypothesis) at decision time; post-decision measurements (FC8 > FC5 in growth, assimilation flux and FA consumption) support but do not prove the burden mechanism.
ddr_annotations.reason_nature_rationale: A mechanistic rationale (expression burden under nutrient limitation) was stated before the action; it is hypothesis-level and was not directly measured (no protein-level or burden quantification reported).

generalizable_rule.statement: In the DH5α-derived engineered E. coli growing solely on CO2 and formic acid, lowering plasmid copy number (low-copy p518FA in FC8) improved growth and C1 assimilation relative to the higher-copy FC5 counterpart, consistent with reducing gene-expression burden under severe nutrient limitation.
generalizable_rule.tested_scope: FC5/FC7/FC8 in M9 + 4.43 g/L sodium formate under 10% CO2/18% O2/72% N2, flask cultivation at 37 °C, 200 r.p.m., 200 h
generalizable_rule.excluded_scope: Other hosts, other pathways or products, other copy-number ranges, and bioreactor conditions were not tested; the expression-burden mechanism was not directly measured.
generalizable_rule.evidence_basis: Fig. 1d growth comparison and Extended Data Fig. 6 assimilation/FA-consumption data; reason_nature=mechanistic_inference (hypothesis-level)

alternatives_considered: Medium-copy (FC7) and low-copy (FC8) variants were both constructed and compared; FC7 grew slightly worse than FC5, FC8 better

ddr_annotations.decision_type_rationale: Q1: deliberate change of cultivation temperature as an engineering variable. Q2: performed in this study. Q3: chosen intervention to suppress filamentation and improve energy efficiency, followed by verification.
ddr_annotations.design_action: Reduce FC8 cultivation temperature from 37 °C to 32 °C (selected after monitoring 30, 32 and 33 °C)
ddr_annotations.design_action_rationale: Lower temperature was expected to increase cytochrome bo (Cyo) and decrease cytochrome bd-I (Cyd) oxidase expression, improving ATP generation efficiency from reducing power.
ddr_annotations.trigger_observation: FC8 cells were filamented when cultured at 37 °C from initial OD600 0.35 and growth stopped at OD600 1.24 (Fig. 2a,b); filamentation was hypothesized to reflect energy deficiency.
ddr_annotations.evidence_grading_rationale: evidence_basis_type=experimental_measurement for the outcome (growth, biomass yield 0.0552±0.0009 vs 0.0365±0.0026 g DCW/g FA, cyoAB/cydAB mRNA shifts at 32 vs 37 °C); the Cyo/Cyd temperature relationship itself is supported by Fig. 2c illustration and Supplementary Note 8 (not provided). Direct ATP/protein-level measurements are not reported.
ddr_annotations.reason_nature_rationale: The energy-deficiency hypothesis and the Cyo/Cyd temperature mechanism were stated before the intervention and are consistent with post-intervention mRNA and yield data; full causal validation (e.g., direct ATP measurement) is not reported.

generalizable_rule.statement: For engineered E. coli FC8 growing solely on CO2 and formic acid, reducing cultivation temperature from 37 °C to 32 °C increased biomass yield on FA, shifted cyoAB/cydAB mRNA in the intended direction, and suppressed cell filamentation.
generalizable_rule.tested_scope: FC8 in M9 + sodium formate under 10% CO2 atmosphere; flask cultivation at 30/32/33 °C compared with 37 °C; bioreactor operated at 32 °C
generalizable_rule.excluded_scope: Other strains/hosts, temperatures outside the tested range, and direct energetic measurements (ATP, proton motive force) were not tested; Cyo/Cyd assessed at mRNA level only.
generalizable_rule.evidence_basis: Fig. 2b-e and Extended Data Fig. 7; reason_nature=mechanistic_inference

alternatives_considered: 30 °C and 33 °C were also monitored; 32 °C gave the highest growth

ddr_annotations.decision_type_rationale: Q1 passes (bioreactor fed-batch setup is an active process intervention), Q2 passes, but Q3 fails: the stated purpose was to determine the maximum achievable OD600 and examine reproducibility — a measurement/demonstration, not a design selection among alternatives. Recorded as validation, not an engineering decision.
ddr_annotations.design_action: Bioreactor fed-batch cultivation of FC8 from high initial OD600 (~1) with pH-stat FA feeding (four independent runs)
ddr_annotations.design_action_rationale: Stated purpose: to determine the maximum achievable OD600 and examine reproducibility.
ddr_annotations.evidence_grading_rationale: Non-decision record; no design rationale to grade.
ddr_annotations.reason_nature_rationale: Not applicable to a validation/measurement record; no design rationale is claimed.

claims.statement: FC5 grew on CO2 and FA alone to OD600 0.285 in 150 h.
FC8 reached maximum OD600 7.38-11.1 across four independent bioreactor cultivations from initial OD600 ~1.
Increasing Cyo and decreasing Cyd levels at 32 °C enhanced energy efficiency, suppressing filamentation by more efficiently converting reducing power to ATP.
claims.boundary: Supported by mRNA ratios and biomass yields; ATP not directly measured; not causally_validated.

claims.statement: The engineered strain shows promise as a platform strain growing on CO2 and FA alone and could enable future bio-based production of chemicals from CO2 and FA.
claims.boundary: Forward-looking claim; no product formation demonstrated in this paper.

claims.statement: Previously reported engineered E. coli strains grew on CO2 and FA only to low final OD600 (up to ~1) (refs 9-11).
claims.boundary: Attributed to cited studies; not experiments of the current article.

source_locations.quote: We engineered Escherichia coli to grow on $\mathbf { c o } _ { 2 }$ and formic acid alone by introducing the synthetic $\mathbf { c o } _ { 2 }$ and formic acid assimilation pathway
Development of an E. coli strain that can efficiently grow to a higher cell density on $\mathrm { C O } _ { 2 }$ and FA alone is needed for industrial biotechnology applications.

We hypothesized that insufficient gluconeogenesis, simultaneous expression of the purT and ftl genes, and inefficient NADPH supply might be the reasons for the inability of the FC1 strain to grow solely on CO and FA.

We then optimized plasmid gene expression levels because excessive gene expression might negatively affect cell growth during limited nutrient supply, especially in a medium containing CO and FA alone.
We hypothesized that cell filamentation might be due to energy deficiency in the cells when growing on CO and FA alone.

First, strain FC1 was constructed by introducing a reconstructed tetrahydrofolate (THF) cycle, reverse glycine cleavage reaction and Candida boidinii Fdh (CbFdh) into the E. coli DH5α\_ GTPS strain (a strain with the gcvR, pflB and serA genes deleted and the native promoter of gcvT replaced with trc; Supplementary Note 3, Extended Data Fig. 1a and Supplementary Table 2).

resulting in strains FC2 (ppsA overexpression and ppsR deletion in FC1), FC3 (purT deletion in FC2) and FC5 (FC3 strain harbouring p100FA2, which additionally expresses the Arabidopsis thaliana $f d h _ { \mathrm { m u t } }$ gene for NADPH generation from FA

Plasmid gene expression levels were fine-tuned by using plasmids with lower copy numbers in FC5 (Fig. 1c) to yield strains FC7 and FC8 (Supplementary Note 7 and Supplementary Table 2), which harboured medium- and low-copy-number plasmids, respectively.
